text:
ashley: quick question — we're debugging a staging model regression and want to persist a hashed snippet of the prompt (not the raw prompt) in staging logs for ~7d to help group failures. Is that allowed? plan: HMAC-SHA256 -> base16, keep prefix only, no raw prompt stored.

michael: what PII surface are we worried about? prompts often contain emails, phone numbers, small bios, etc.

ashley: yep — that's the main concern. our idea is: apply a lightweight scrub (regex for emails/phones) then hash. we won't include user id or email fields in the same record.

jordan (security): high level: ok in staging if we do one-way HMAC with a KMS-managed key (no app-baked salts). Requirements: rotate keys per policy, enforce allowlist for who can query/stage logs, audit every access, and retention = 7 days by default. Also prefer storing a truncated hex digest (to reduce accidental linkage) rather than full digest.

michael: truncation tradeoff — too short increases collisions. For grouping we need some entropy. Suggest 16 hex chars (64 bits) as a compromise.

jordan (security): 16 hex (64 bits) is reasonable for staging grouping. Also: ensure the scrub runs before hashing (do not hash then scrub), and capture the scrubbed->hashed pipeline in CI tests. No reversible transforms.

ashley: noted. Implementation plan: 1) run regex scrub for emails/phones, fallback to mask patterns; 2) HMAC-SHA256 via KMS; 3) store first 16 hex chars and a flag `scrubbed:true`; 4) logs written to staging S3 with SSE-KMS; 5) retention lifecycle 7 days. Will open allowlist request for eng-sre + eng-ml and attach audit justification.

jordan (security): add a short doc in devdocs/log-redaction.md that records the regex, KMS key id, retention, and allowlist process. I can approve once docs + CI tests exist. Also file SEC ticket to track: SEC-7231.

audit-bot: access request created: https://tickets.redwood/SEC-7231 (requester: ashley)

ashley: thanks — I'll push the PR for code + docs + test, then request the allowlist. will ping here when it's ready :thumbsup:
